post.caption: Palladium is named for an asteroid. Heinrich Olbers found the asteroid Pallas in March 1802. The asteroid is named for the goddess Pallas Athena. Around 1802 the chemist William Wollaston named his new metal after it. In 1803 he sold it anonymously as Palladium, or New Silver. A rival chemist called it an alloy of platinum and mercury. Wollaston offered 20 pounds to anyone who could make it. Nobody did. It is naturally white and the lightest metal in the platinum group. Jewelers began using it around 1939, when platinum was needed for war. A 950 stamp means the piece is 95 percent palladium.
